record.biographicalNote:
Otis Ray Bowen was born February 26, 1918, near Leiter's Ford, Indiana to Vernie Bowen and Pearl Irene Wright. He graduated from Indiana University with an AB in 1939 and MD in 1942. He married Elizabeth Ann Steinmann in 1939.  Following her death in 1981, on 26 September 1981 he married Rose May Hochstetler.

He began his medical career on an internship from Memorial Hospital in South Bend, Indiana in 1942. From 1943 to 1946 he served in the Medical Corps of the U.S. Army, rising from the rank of 1st lieutenant to captain. On his return from World War II he set up his own medical practice in his home town of Bremen, Indiana, which he discontinued in 1972. During this time he also was a member of staff for various hospitals in Indiana and, in 1952, was elected coroner of Marshall County, Indiana. In 1976 he took up the post of clinical professor of family medicine at Indiana University.  From 1978 to 1985 he served as a trustee of Valparaiso University.

He served as a member of the Indiana House of Representatives from 1956 to 1958 and again from 1960 to 1972. He was speaker of the house from 1967 to 1972, Vice Chairman of the legislative council from 1967 to 1968, and Chairman until 1972. After his unsuccessful attempt in 1968 he was elected Governor of Indiana in 1972 and was re-elected for a second term in 1976. As Governor he initiated a tax restructuring, and developed a state-wide emergency medical services system. He served as Secretary of Health and Human Services from December 13, 1985 to January 20, 1989, making him the first medical doctor to serve in this position. Following his government service, he retired to his home in Bremen, Indiana.

Bowen served on a number of committees and conferences, including the Education Commission of the States, Republican Governors Conference, and the President's Commission on Federalism. He has also received various awards, including the George F. Hixson award from Kiwanis International.

record.biographicalNote:
Gloria Swanson was an actress and icon during the silent era of motion pictures.  She was born Gloria May Josephine Svensson (some sources say Swenson) on March 27, 1899.  She changed her name to Gloria Swanson in 1916, and married Wallace Beery the same year.  They divorced in 1919.  She rose to stardom in the silent films of the early 1920s.  In December 1919 she married Herbert K. Somborn, but they divorced in 1925, and on January 28, 1925 she married Marquis Henri de la Falaise de la Coudraye.  In 1926, Swanson joined Mary Pickford, Douglas Fairbanks, Charlie Chaplin, and others in forming United Artists (UA), a film distribution company.  She also created Gloria Swanson Productions for her own films, which were then distributed by UA, but her company was dissolved in 1932.

In November 1927, Swanson met Joseph P. Kennedy and they began an affair.  Kennedy took charge of her film career and helped her make the film Sadie Thompson (1928), for which she won and Academy Award nomination.  Swanson and Kennedy eventually became estranged.  In 1930, she divorced the marquis and on August 16, 1931 she married Michael Farmer.  They divorced in 1934.  She starred in her first sound film in 1929, The Trespasser, which won her an Academy Away nomination.  She starred in various other films throughout the 1930s.  In 1945 she was married for one month to William Davey; they officially divorced three years later.  In 1948 she had her own talk show on television, The Gloria Swanson Hour.

In 1950, Swanson starred in Billy Wilder's production, Sunset Boulevard, which won her another Academy Award nomination.  For many years she remained working in theater, radio, and television, as well as having other interests.  In 1957 she created and sold her own line of clothing.  In 1976 she married William Duffy, whom she divorced in 1981.  She died in New York City on April 4, 1983.

record.biographicalNote: Thomas Bernard Larkin (1890-1968) was born in Louisburg, Wisconsin. B.A. He received his commission in the Corps of Engineers from West Point in 1915, and served with the Punitive Expedition into Mexico in 1916 and 1917. He served with the AEF in World War I, then served as assistant military attaché in Tokyo from 1921 to 1923.  He graduated from Army Industrial College in 1927, then the Command and General Staff School in 1929, the Army War College in 1938 and the Naval War College in 1939. He was officer in charge of the third locks project at the Panama Canal from 1939 to 1942, and reached the rank of brigadier general in May 1942. He was chief engineer, then chief of staff at Services of Supply in the Mediterranean Theater of Operations in 1942 and 1943, reaching the rank of major general in April 1943. He was commanding general of 2nd Service Command, Mediterranean Theater of Operations in 1945 and 1946. After the World War II, he was quartermaster general of the Army from 1946 to 1949 and deputy chief of staff for logistics of the U.S. Army from 1949 to 1952. He retired from Army service in December 1952.

Francis Thomas “Frank” Hoban (b. November 30, 1935, Minersville, Pennsylvania-d. December 5, 2002, Gettysburg, Pennsylvania) was an executive at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) for 34 years. He held several positions during his tenure at NASA including Assistant Executive Secretary (1970-1973); Director of Business Practices for Low Cost Systems Office (1973-1976); Civil Service Reform Act Implementation Task Force (1977-1979); Space Station Task Force (1982-1986), and head of Program and Project Management Training and Development Initiatives (1986-1994).

After he retired from NASA in 1994, Hoban joined GMU as a senior fellow at its Institute of Public Policy. In 1998, he retired and became director of the NASA-GMU Continuing Career Program, which was an initiative to target senior NASA scientists and managers nearing retirement age as a resource for commercial space and technology companies

record.biographicalNote: Mortimer M. Caplin (b. July 11, 1916, New York, N.Y.-d. July 15, 2009, Chevy Chase, Maryland) was an attorney and educator. He was in private legal practice in New York from 1941 to 1950, with a break for service in the U.S. Navy during World War II, and was a professor of law at the University of Virginia for over 30 years starting in 1950. Caplin served on the President's Task Force on Taxation and was Commissioner of Internal Revenue from February 7, 1961 to July 10, 1964. In 1964, he became a founding member of the law firm of Caplin & Drysdale, Chartered.

record.biographicalNote: Philip Weiser served in the Obama Administration as senior advisor for technology and innovation to the National Economic Council, in 2010, and in 2009 as Deputy Assistant Attorney General in the United State’s Justice Department's Antitrust Division. record.biographicalNote: Deborah D. Pryce (1951- ) was a Representative from Ohio. She was born in Warren, Trumbull County, Ohio, on July 29, 1951. Pryce graduated from Champion High School, Warren, Ohio, 1969; B.A., Ohio State University, Columbus, Ohio, 1973; and J.D., Capital University, Columbus, Ohio, 1976. Pryce was elected as a Republican to the 103rd and to the seven succeeding Congresses (January 3, 1993-January 3, 2009); was not a candidate for reelection to the 111th Congress in 2008; and was House Republican Conference Chair (108th-109th Congress).

record.biographicalNote: Katja Bullock (b. March 15, 1943) was born and raised in Germany. She received her Bachelor of Science degree equivalent from Berufs-Hochschule at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg. Bullock emigrated to the United States in 1965 and upon arrival became interested in American politics. She became a citizen and registered to vote so that she could participate in American democracy. After 1976, Ms. Bullock was regularly involved in presidential campaigns as a volunteer or a paid staffer. Ms. Bullock worked in The White House for President Trump, serving as a Special Assistant to the President for Presidential Personnel and Director of Operations of that same office. She held similar positions and duties in the Administrations of Presidents Reagan and George H.W. Bush.
